system_overview: This specification implements and verifies the lexicographically-least circular substring algorithm from the 1980 paper by Kellogg S. Booth (Information Processing Letters, doi:10.1016/0020-0190(80)90149-0). Given a string viewed as circular (where the end wraps around to the beginning), the algorithm finds the rotation that produces the lexicographically smallest string. The algorithm runs in linear time by building a failure function similar to the one used in the Knuth-Morris-Pratt string matching algorithm.
actors_and_components: There are no concurrent actors. The specification models a single sequential algorithm that processes a circular string. The main components are: the input string (a zero-indexed sequence of characters from a finite character set that is a subset of the natural numbers), a failure function array used to track pattern-matching information, and loop control variables that drive the algorithm through its nested loops.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the input string, a zero-indexed sequence of characters chosen nondeterministically from all possible sequences over the character set (the corpus); (2) the length of the input string; (3) a failure function array indexed from 0 to twice the string length, initialized to a sentinel value meaning undefined; (4) a pattern-match index tracking the current failure function lookup; (5) an outer loop counter running from 1 to just below twice the string length; (6) the current best rotation offset, indicating the start position of the lexicographically smallest rotation found so far; (7) a program counter tracking which labeled step of the algorithm is executing.
initial_state: The input string is chosen nondeterministically from all zero-indexed sequences over the character set. The string length is set to the length of the chosen string. The failure function is initialized so every entry maps to the sentinel value. The pattern-match index starts at the sentinel value. The outer loop counter starts at 1. The best rotation offset starts at 0. The program counter starts at the outer loop entry.
actions: The algorithm proceeds through labeled steps in a sequential loop structure: (1) Outer loop check: if the loop counter is below twice the string length, continue; otherwise terminate. (2) Failure function lookup: retrieve the failure function value for the current position relative to the best offset. (3) Inner comparison loop: compare the character at the current loop position (modulo string length) with the character at the candidate position (modulo string length). If they differ and the pattern-match index is not the sentinel value, continue the inner loop; otherwise exit to the post-comparison step. (4) If the current character is less than the candidate character during the inner loop, update the best rotation offset. (5) Follow the failure function chain by setting the pattern-match index to its failure function value. (6) Post-comparison: if the characters still differ and the pattern-match index is the sentinel value, check again if the current character is less, and if so update the best offset. Set the failure function entry to the sentinel (resetting it) or to one plus the pattern-match index (extending the match). (7) Increment the loop counter and return to the outer loop check. A stuttering action allows the algorithm to remain in its final state after termination.
safety_properties: Type invariant: the input string remains in the corpus, the string length equals the length of the input, the failure function maps to valid indices or the sentinel, the pattern-match index and loop counter are within valid ranges, and the best rotation offset is a valid index of the input string. Correctness: upon termination, the best rotation offset identifies the lexicographically-minimal rotation of the input string -- the rotation at that offset is less than or equal to all other rotations, and among rotations producing the same sequence, it has the smallest shift value.
liveness_properties: Termination: the algorithm eventually reaches the terminated state.
model_bounds: The character set is a constant that must be a subset of the natural numbers. For model checking, the character set size and maximum string length are configured via a separate model-checking module. The state space grows with both the alphabet size and string length.
additional_assumptions: The specification uses zero-indexed sequences (defined in a separate utility module) rather than the standard one-indexed sequences. The circular nature of the string is handled by indexing modulo the string length. The algorithm processes a doubled string (iterating up to twice the string length) to handle the wrap-around without explicit circular indexing logic. The nondeterministic choice of input string means the model checker verifies correctness for all strings over the character set up to the configured maximum length.
